definition: Resonate means to stir a deep and lasting sense of connection.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word resonate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know resonate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The night-shift nurse never guessed a picture book about moving day would resonate so with her young patients; three families have asked to keep the copy.
To appeal is a fainter thing than to resonate — a poster can appeal to you and be forgotten by dinner.
Haunt goes further than resonate: what resonates keeps meaning something to you, while what haunts you follows you into quiet moments uninvited.

To strike a chord is to connect at once with someone's feelings — the phrase names the instant of recognition, the nod in the moment. To resonate asks what happens afterward: the connection must run deep and keep lasting. Plenty of ads strike a chord on first viewing; far fewer still resonate a month later.

To ring true is to feel accurate to your own experience — a matter of believability, the detail that sounds exactly right. To resonate goes past accuracy into attachment: the thing stirs a deep and lasting connection. A crime drama can ring true without moving anyone; what resonates keeps mattering after the credits.
